Added

  • **Hermes fidelity is tested through the running agent, not inferred from route health.** Spire now verifies authenticated Hermes readiness, repairs the upstream MCP registry through its dashboard control plane when needed, and exercises tool selection, tool-result replay, reasoning, usage, streaming, and structured errors as separate live obligations. Provider refusal preservation remains visibly unqualified instead of being silently counted as passed.
  • **llama.cpp engine upgrades are first-class model-lifecycle operations.** The app, CLI, MCP, and fingerprint-bound fleet path can deep-verify an existing managed artifact, admit the new engine against a side-by-side endpoint, rerun the stored policy, promote only after acceptance, and restore the previous engine executable, receipt, and endpoint on failure. Before any lifecycle mutation, Spire copies the signed predecessor engine into owner-only managed storage, binds its bytes and version evidence to a receipt, and thereafter resolves launches by the placement's engine tag. Existing weights are reused by content address; Spire does not copy the 0731 model to perform an engine upgrade.

Corrected

  • **DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 uses its exact upstream protocol contract.** Spire now pins llama.cpp v0.4.0 at commit 5266f24da75dc449bd56cbed7addb9c8e4a6a73e, embeds and digest-verifies llama.cpp's exact DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 chat template, selects DeepSeek reasoning explicitly, and applies the model publisher's maximum-reasoning and agentic sampling defaults. A missing or altered template stops the launch before model memory is touched.
  • **llama.cpp build provenance fails closed.** Reused helpers must match their recorded binary digest, source digest, commit, and self-reported version. Every real compilation starts from a fresh extraction of the verified source archive and an empty CMake tree, preventing edited source or stale objects from inheriting the lock's identity.
  • **Hermes installation remains actionable in the Chat window.** The surface now performs its automatic availability check once per presentation instead of restarting the check whenever the result changes the rendered state. The official-image installation action therefore stays visible and can be completed by the operator.
  • **Model endpoints fail fast on real port conflicts.** Spire retains oMLX's pre-spawn owner check but reads macOS's bounded kernel listener table, avoiding lsof process scans that can hang past the lifecycle deadline while still naming the process and PID that owns a requested port.
  • **Local Cortex gateways work without weakening web transport security.** The signed Mac app now declares Apple's scoped local-network transport boundary, allowing an operator-entered private IPv4, IPv6, or .local gateway while leaving arbitrary HTTP loads disabled. The XcodeGen authority also owns the app's source-revision plist field so regeneration cannot silently remove release provenance.

Added

  • **Federated Mac operations from the Spire window.** A Mac can be discovered, paired with continuity checks, inspected, updated through the signed channel, and used for managed model lifecycle work without controller-side application replacement. Remote actions negotiate the MCP protocol, verify the exact Spire source and management executable, and fail closed when the peer is incompatible or its identity changes.
  • **Managed GGUF lifecycle and admission.** Placement now records immutable source, shard and engine evidence; supports recoverable download, reclaim, activate, unload, rollback and maintenance transitions; and exposes one admission policy across the app, CLI, MCP and fleet. DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 is represented as its complete five-shard deployment rather than one conveniently visible file.
  • **Hermes gateway qualification.** Spire can prepare the upstream Hermes Agent runtime, bind its model profile to a Cortex gateway, verify authentication and route metadata separately from the physical model receipt on King, and present actionable qualification failures in the app.
  • **Apple-silicon fleet telemetry.** The app now carries a digest-pinned mactop producer and reports CPU, pressure-oriented memory, resident/reclaimable host memory, disk, thermal, fan, accelerator and model-process measurements with sample time and provenance.

Security

  • **Secrets no longer appear in container or child-process metadata.** Spire materializes owner-only secret files, mounts them read-only into Apple containers, and passes MCP bearer credentials by file. Unsafe identifiers, symlinks, permissive files, empty values and oversized material are rejected before launch.

Corrected

  • **Trusted fleet controls retain least privilege without becoming inert.** The general MCP server still honors the read-only agent policy, while a fingerprint-bound fleet operation now receives a process-scoped operator broker only after node, source, executable, and SSH host-key continuity pass. Confirmed GUI lifecycle actions no longer fail because the remote owner was launched with read-only grants, and the elevated posture is never written into the Mac's standing agent policy.
  • **Observed fleet placements now become the endpoints the operator manages.** The Server screen reconciles each fingerprint-bound llama.cpp placement into its local endpoint catalog using the exact case-sensitive runtime role, model, port, revision, and context. It replaces only the untouched placeholder, preserves configured stopped endpoints, and no longer shows a fictional endpoint-1 while a different model is serving on the Mac.
  • **System RAM provenance.** mactop's memory.used excludes inactive pages, including clean memory-mapped model weights. Spire now keeps that pressure signal while separately reporting Mach resident/reclaimable host memory and PID-bound model artifact, RSS, mapped residency, physical footprint, and an identified LocalAI-derived planning estimate. Unsupported sensors and stale samples display as unavailable instead of zero or old data, raw process inventories are not persisted, and model bytes are exposed only after current files match the placement receipt.
  • **Lifecycle recovery is stateful and fail-closed.** Interrupted placement and reclaim work keeps a durable journal, preserves the last verified deployment, refuses corrupt state, and reports recovery work instead of treating a running process as sufficient proof.
  • **Fleet updates preserve model availability.** A suspended model must exit before replacement continues, readiness is parsed as structured evidence, and the update path works under zsh on Macs with or without persistent llama roles.
  • **Headless pairing keeps one permanent node identity.** The app, CLI, and SSH-owned MCP server now share a locked owner-only identity file instead of asking a login Keychain to serve a session with no UI. A readable legacy Keychain identity migrates without rotation; ambiguous Keychain denial fails closed, and concurrent first use converges on one key.
  • **Privileged updates preserve model-registry access.** A system-daemon reinstall now returns every known model-state artifact and its advisory lock to the unprivileged serving account. The handoff uses symlink-safe ownership changes and fails the install if it cannot restore the boundary, preventing a successful update from leaving the app and MCP unable to read models.
  • **Fleet identity does not depend on reverse DNS.** Node status reads the kernel hostname directly instead of asking Foundation's NSHost to resolve the current machine. A headless Mac with no reverse-DNS answer can now finish the SSH/MCP pairing request within its bounded deadline.
  • **Fleet identity dates use one wire format.** MCP now emits ISO 8601 dates, matching the app and trusted fleet decoder. Pairing no longer rejects a prompt and authentic node-status response because the server encoded its timestamp as Foundation's private reference-date number.

The agent's own home, hosted — and plugins.

Added

  • **The agent on the Spire home**: Spire now starts the installed Hermes Agent's own dashboard and hosts it right on the home page — chat, sessions, profiles, models, all of Hermes's own surfaces in Spire's window. Spire supervises the process and provides the window; it builds none of what's inside.
  • **Plugins**: Spire gains a plugin structure mirroring Hermes's own — one folder per plugin in Spire's data directory with a small manifest, all data, never code changes. Hermes is the first plugin; its manifest declares how it runs and what it provides, and you can edit it.

Every dialog gets a small question mark.

Added

  • **The question mark**: dialogs stay clear and concise, and a small question-mark button expands the fuller story — what happened technically, what the remedy button will actually do, and where the log lives. First on the error console; every new dialog adopts it as law.
  • The error report now carries its technical rendering behind the question mark instead of burying it or dumping it in your face.

You land on Spire: the crossbar is the app's map.

Added

  • **The crossbar**: the front page now reads Spire · System · Federation · Endpoints · Applications · Models, and the app lands on Spire.
  • **The Spire home**: cards that map to the crossbar — the System card (with the desktop-computer symbol) shows this machine's live CPU, RAM, DISK and uptime in stat tiles; Federation, Endpoints, Applications, and Models cards each summarize their surface. Clicking a card goes where its tab goes.
  • **The System tab**: the machine the application is on — CPU, RAM, Thermal, Disk, and uptime, live, from the system's own counters.
  • **The Models tab**: Place a Model and what's placed, as its own door.
